pages.text: Thermia has an interior system, Using flood fill and allowing for quite large and dynamic structures. The system uses the flood fill data to calculate internal thermodynamics, In short hot things warm the space over time and cold things absorb heat over time. Some blocks have a block seal, This metric is a measure of how leaky a block is and while in an external wall allows heat transfer between the interior and environment.

Creating an interior is fairly simple. All you need is a enclosed space of any material, and a block with the thermia:interior_triggers tag. (By default a normal or thatch bed.) Shift right click the trigger block to trigger the interior creation.
pages.title: Creating an Interior

pages.text: Example house with open and closed trapdoors and a thatch bed.

The block seal metric is a measure of how sealed or leaky a block is, For instance a half slab side on has a block seal of 0.5. It also supports block states allowing for multiple block seal values based on state such as trapdoors open or closed. This value along side wind is used to calculate how much pull the external environment has.
pages.title: Block Seal

pages.text: Interiors will feed their temperature back into TFC, This will allow TFC and other mods to use the interior temperature for things like crops.
pages.title: Terrafirmacraft Temperature

pages.text: Just like entity heat sources, They are blocks/fluids with temperature above 0. Interiors have a realistic thermodynamics and can take a while to fully warm requiring vast energy, Remember this when building your base. The sun can also heat your interior through transparent blocks, So if you build is cold try adding large windows.
pages.title: Heat Sources

pages.text: Heat sinks are blocks/fluids with a temperature below 0. While a heat source pulls an interior temperature up, Sinks polls them down.
pages.title: Heat Sinks
